2_Introduction: The combined treatment featured a PCE of 19.4%, FF of 73.62%, Voc of 1.1038 V, and Jsc of 23.87 mA/cm². The perovskite precursor solutions were prepared by dissolving 1.73 mol/L Cs0.05MA0.16FA0.79Pb1I2.9Br0.1. The perovskite solution was spin-coated in two steps, namely 1000 rpm for 15 s and 5000 rpm for 30 s. During the spin-coating process, 180 µL of CB was dropped on the perovskite at 10 s, prior to the end of the second procedure. The substrates were sequentially heated at 105 °C for 30 min for perovskite crystal formation. XRD analysis showed a diffraction peak was identified at 4.00°, with an intensity of 71.75 cts，which corresponds to the formation of a 2D structure within the perovskite lattice. The high intensity implies efficient surface passivation, contributing positively to device performance. GIXRD analysis further revealed a residual tensile stress of 10.50 MPa in the perovskite film via measurement conducted at an incident angle of 1°.
3_Result_Discussion: The perovskite layer, formulated as Cs₀.₀₅MA₀.₁₆FA₀.₇₉PbI₂.₉Br₀.₁, adopts a mixed-cation A-site configuration that enhances phase stability and suppresses halide segregation by optimizing the Goldschmidt tolerance factor (~0.98), while the partial Br⁻ substitution at the X-site widens the bandgap slightly and mitigates iodide vacancy formation; its crystallization is precisely governed by the two-step spin-coating protocol—initial low-speed deposition (1000 rpm, 15 s) enabling uniform wet-film formation and interfacial wetting, followed by high-speed crystallization (5000 rpm, 30 s) with antisolvent quenching (180 µL chlorobenzene at 10 s) that triggers rapid nucleation and arrests Ostwald ripening, thereby yielding compact, pinhole-free films with suppressed PbI₂ residual phases and reduced deep-level trap states at grain boundaries and surfaces; the subsequent 105 °C annealing for 30 min promotes complete ligand exchange, volatilizes excess organic species, and facilitates strain relaxation—yet GIXRD quantifies a residual tensile stress of 10.50 MPa, indicating incomplete lattice relaxation that would otherwise induce microcracking and non-radiative recombination centers; critically, the XRD-detectable diffraction peak at 4.00° with high intensity (71.75 cts) unambiguously confirms the in situ formation of a low-n (n = 1 or 2) 2D perovskite phase at the surface or grain boundaries, acting as a self-assembled passivating capping layer that electronically decouples surface defects, suppresses ion migration via steric and energetic barriers, and modulates interfacial energy alignment to minimize electron extraction losses—this structural signature, corroborated by the absence of parasitic PbI₂ peaks near 12.6°, demonstrates effective suppression of both undercoordinated Pb²⁺ and I⁻ vacancies, directly translating into enhanced carrier lifetime and reduced interfacial recombination, as further implied by the high PL quantum yield expected from such a phase-pure, low-strain, 2D/3D heterostructured film; collectively, the synergistic interplay between compositional engineering, kinetic crystallization control, and emergent 2D phase passivation yields optimized charge transport pathways, minimized non-radiative voltage losses, and robust morphological continuity—resulting in a Voc of 1.1038 V, Jsc of 23.87 mA/cm², FF of 73.62%, and PCE of 19.4%.
